RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the August 26, 2004/Bhadrapada 4, 1926 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Agro and Rural Industries; Atomic Energy;
Coal and Mines; Communications and Information Technology;
 External Affairs; Labour and Employment; Non-Resident Indians
Affairs; Ocean Development; Personnel, Public Grievances and
 Pensions; Planning; Road Transport and Highways; Science and
Technology; Shipping; Small Scale Industries; Space; Statistics
 and Programme Implementation)
Total number of questions — 20
Social Security Schemes under EPFO
*441. SHRI DIPANKAR MUKHERJEE:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had designated
the Employees Provident Fund
Organisation (EPFO) as the nodal agency
for administering social security schemes
in the country; and
(b) whether the EPFO, as a nodal
agency, has been authorised to issue
National Social Security Numbers to the
workers covered under various social
security schemes?
Services for accident victims on
Highways
*442. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the NHAI
Project Office in Rajahmundry has
received offers of help from NGOs and
others to attend on accident victims and
also provide First Aid, etc. on major
Highways like NH-5;
(b) if so, the details thereof and whether
any action has been initiated in this matter;
(c) whether it is a fact that the NHAI
has not reacted to such offers; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps proposed to be taken to immediately
attend to such offers?
Labour laws on LPG distributors
†*443. SHRI RAM NATH KOVIND:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Labour laws like State
Insurance Corporation and Provident Fund
laws have been enforced on LPG
distributors; and
(b) the grounds on which these labour
laws have been enforced?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

134
Express lane on NH-9
*444. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether representation has been
received to take up expeditious completion
of the four lane express way on NH-9 from
Hyderabad to Vijayawada which is vital
from business and commercial point of view;
and
(b) if so, the action proposed to
complete the project early to avoid 30 to
40 accidents taking place daily due to heavy
traffic?
Civil Services Reforms
*445. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Committee on Civil
Services Reforms headed by Shri P.C. Hota
has submitted its report to the Union
Cabinet Secretary on the 30th July, 2004;
(b) if so, the salient features of the
recommendations made by the Committee
in its report; and
(c) the reaction of Government thereto?
Death of lab animals at ITRC,
Lucknow
*446. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether due to failure of air
conditioning system in June last about 700
lab animals died in the newly constructed
modern laboratory of Industrial and
Toxicology Research Centre of CSIR at
Lucknow;
(b) if so, whether the cause of the
failure of the air-conditioning system has
been investigated, if so, the details
thereof;
(c) the extent of financial loss caused to
the research centre due to the incident; and
(d) the action taken to prevent such
incidents and also against those found
negligent in the discharge of their duty in
this incident?
Release of Indian hostages/captives in
Iraq
†*447. SHRI PYARELAL KHAN-
DELWAL: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a state of
confusion prevailed regarding release of
Indian hostages in Iraq only due to the
evasive policy of Government;
(b) whether it is also a fact that a large
number of Indian Nationals are still
working in American Military camps as
captives;
(c) if so, the details thereof and by when
Government would bring them back to
India;
(d) whether Indian Embassy in Iraq
remained a silent spectator in this case; and
(e) if not, the details of action taken by
it?
Indians in foreign jails
† *448. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Indians lodged in
foreign jails, country-wise;
(b) whether any steps are being taken
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

135
by Government to get them released; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Delinking of Vadinar area from
Kandla Port Trust
*449. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRI LEKHRAJ BACHANI:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken any
final decision on the long outstanding
request of the Government of Gujarat to
delink Vadinar area from the port limits of
the Kandla Port Trust and return it back to
the State Government;
(b) if so, the decision taken by
Government in this regard; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to
compensate the Government of Gujarat for
the commercial loss, in case its proposal is
not acceptable?
Declaration of certain roads as
National Highways
†*450. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any scheme under
consideration to declare the road from
Sujangarh to Salasar-Sikar-Neem Ka
Thana-Kotputli-Behrod-Alwar-Nagaur-
Theeg-Mathura on Ambala-Hissar-Churu-
Fatehpur-Sujangarh-Nagaur-Jodhpur Pali
National Highway as a National Highway;
(b) whether there is need to declare the
road from Kolayal to Mathura as National
Highway by linking Sujangarh-Mukam-
Nokha-Kolayal road with the road
mentioned in part (a) above; and
(c) whether this road would be
developed as toll road by declaring it a
National Highway?
Memorandum from Chief Minister of
Madhya Pradesh
†*451. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Chief Minister of
Madhya Pradesh had submitted a
memorandum to Honourable Prime
Minister wherein main problems of
Madhya Pradesh have been mentioned;
(b) if so, the details of the action taken
by the Government in this regard alongwith
its present status; and
(c) if no action has been taken so far,
by when the same would be taken?
Land for the unemployed
†*452. SHRI ISAM SINGH: Will the
Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether 2/3rd  part of cultivable
plain land in the country is lying unused
with the Government; and
(b) if so, what is the plan of Government
to provide employment to the unemployed
persons from out of the said land?
Agro-based Industries in Uttaranchal
†*453. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will
the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the number of small and tiny agro
based industries alongwith the number of
persons employed therein in Uttaranchal;
(b) whether Government are aware of
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

136
the fact that a large number of such small
cottage and rural industries have been
closed down during last few years; and
(c) if so, the number of industries so
closed and the number of persons rendered
unemployed as a result thereof?
Modernisation of Postal Department
*454. SHRIMATI  N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) what measures the Department of
Posts is taking towards its modernisation;
(b) how optimally the Department of
Posts is utilising the V-Sats;
(c) the details of the centres that are
covered by V-Sat in the country,  State-
wise; and
(d) what sort of business the
Department of Posts is looking for, apart
from regular post and e-post?
India's investment in communication
sector abroad
*455. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government plan to invest
in foreign countries in the communication
sector;
(b) if so, whether any agreement has
been signed or consultation is in progress
with the foreign countries in this regard;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of the communication
projects of Indian-origin companies in the
foreign countries?
Ban on outdoor use of products
*456. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. VIJAY MALLYA:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether a ban exists as of today, on
outdoor use of products (based on
international standard IEEE 802.11b) for
wireless networking and transfer of data
between computers;
(b) if so, whether Government consider
any merit in continuing such ban; and
(c) if not, by when, Government plan
to lift the ban?
Implementation of schemes for
reviving projects
*457. SHRI R.P. GOENKA: Will the
Minister of STATISTICS AND
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
major projects, above Rs. 100 crores, which
in terms of the value of investment add up
to about Rs. 50,000 crores, have been either
stalled or deferred indefinitely in various
States;
(b) if so, the details thereof, and the
reasons therefor, State-wise; and
(c) the steps being taken to implement
and/or modify the schemes so as to utilise
the scarce national resources in a more
judicious manner for fruitful results?
Disrupted telephones in Pauri Garhwal
*458. SHRI DARA SINGH
CHAUHAN: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFOR-
MATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to
state:

137
(a) whether Government are aware that
the telephone facilities provided in the
villages of District Pauri Garhwal remained
totally disrupted for long periods during
the months of May and June, 2004 despite
consumers having made several complaints
for smooth services, particularly in Patti
Edwal Syun, Pauri Garhwal;
(b) whether it is a fact that Telephone
Exchange situated at Gurduri is completely
out of order and telephone lines of this
exchange are frequently out of service; and
(c) whether Government have taken
any action so that villagers get proper
benefits of telephone services and ensure
good telephone services for remote areas?
Improvement of rural roads
*459. DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
SHRIMATI PREMA
    CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to focus on rural roads and the
implementation of the National Highways
Development Project envisaged by earlier
Government would not be provided much
financial assistance;
(b) if so, whether 7300 KM which was
to be taken up under Rs. 30,000 crores
second phase of NHDP, work on only 596
KMs has been completed;
(c) whether Government propose to
improve the rural roads instead of National
Highways Development Project; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
total rural roads that would be under taken
during 2004-05?
Manpower Export Promotion Council
*460. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
SHRI SUDARSHAN
AKARAPU:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government  have set-up a
Manpower Export Promotion Council to
regulate hiring practices for overseas jobs;
(b) if so, whether there is proposal to
open a nodal office for the Council in
Delhi;
(c) whether his Ministry has been asked
to set-up a welfare fund for the Indian
diaspora in various countries; and
(d) if so, what are other steps
Government proposed to take to promote
multidimensional welfare of NRI including
workers of  Gulf countries?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 20th August, 2004 Secretary-General.

Employment generation through
rural industrialisation
†2383. SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
boost up rural industrialisation with the
help of private and public sectors for
uplifting the rural standard of living and
generating more opportunities of
employment by establishing better co-
ordination between towns and villages;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when the final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?
Labour migration

Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that due to inadequate agro-based
industries a large scale of labour migration
is occurring in Chhattisgarh to other States
leading to their exploitation in those States;
(b) whether Government propose to
establish some agro-based industries to
arrest large scale of labour migration; and
(c) if so, the number and details of the
industries that are proposed or have been
established so far in the State?
KVIC units in Uttaranchal

the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the units set up in
Uttaranchal by the Khadi and Village
Industries Commission  (KVIC) during the
last three years, year-wise;
(b) whether some of the units already
set up by the KVIC in this State have been
closed;
(c) if so, the total number of the units
closed;
(d) whether Government have fixed any

Financial conditions of farmers
†2386. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P.
GOYAL: Will the Minister of AGRO AND
RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any plan to establish agriculture
based industries to provide technical
training for it as well as to provide financial
assistance for the establishment of
industries to farmers in order to bring

Revolving funds for training rural

2387. SHRI K. B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of AGRO

(a) whether the State Government of
Karnataka has sought Central assistance

Crisis in the Coir Industry
2388. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government  are aware of
the fact that the Coir Industry is facing
serious crisis;
(b) whether Government have
contemplated any comprehensive plan to
tide over the crisis;
(c) whether Government have taken
initiative to put coir as an agricultural
product in the WTO list; and
(d) if so, the details and the results of
such initiatives?
Duties of Coir Board in Andhra
Pradesh
2389. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have assigned
specific duties to the Coir Board to help
coconut growers;
(b) to what extent the Coir Board has
made its presence felt in Andhra Pradesh;
(c) the details of such work done by the
Coir Board in helping farmers of Andhra
Pradesh in the year 2003-04;
(d) whether any funds were made
available by the Coir Board in that period;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Exploration of Mineral Sand in

MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the stage at which the joint venture

KSIDC for the exploration of mineral sand
of chavara in Kerala stands at present; and
(b) the progress attained in the proposal
so far?

533
Nuclear Island
2391. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
to make "Koodankulam" a Nuclear Island;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when, the Koodankulam Atomic
Power Station would start supplying
power and what would be its capacity?

(d) by when all the Officials/Engineers

Minimum wages for labours of

minimum wages;
(b) whether  it is also a fact that they
are being denied other statutory benefits
too; and
(c) if so, reactions of Government in
the matter?

Amendment Bill

(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) Government's reaction on this
demand; and
(d) the points of the said bill on which
objections are being raised and the reasons
therefor?
Coal Mines Nationalisation
(Amendment) Bill

the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government

coal blocks to private companies for captive

(b) if so, the salient features of the

(c) whether consultations have been
made with the representatives concerned
in this regard; and
(d) if so, the outcome of the
consultations?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Use of obsolete technology in mining
2396. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Rs. 4000
crores of FDI has been approved in the
mining sector, recently;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that due to
obsolete technology used by Indian miners,
the country has been deficient in high-value
minerals; and
(d) the total mineral production of the
country during the last three years;
year-wise?
Cooking Coal reserves
2397. SHRI R. K. ANAND: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that good quality
cooking coal reserves have depleted and
the washeries are not getting coal of superior
quality in desired quantity to yield clean
coal; and
(b) if so, the action Government
propose to take in the matter?
Private investment in mines and
minerals sector
†2398. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have allowed
private investment in mines and minerals
sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Losses to ECL, BCCL and CCL
†2399. SHRI P. K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether E.C.L., B.C.C.L. and
C.C.L. are suffering losses continuously
for the last three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) in what manner Government
contemplate to solve this problem?

Neyveli

state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the royalty
for mining of Lignite at Neyveli in Tamil
Nadu was taken several years in advance
by the Government of Tamil Nadu during
1996—2001;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the royalty for Lignite due to be
given to Tamil Nadu as on date?
Illegal occupation of SECL land
†2401. SHRI RAMADHAR
KASHYAP: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) the names of the persons who have
illegally occupied the S.E.C.L. land in
Ghevra/Dipika area alongwith the area
thereof; and
(b) the action taken by S.E.C.L. to get
the land vacated?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

535
Privatisation of Coal mining

SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Coal users make a strong
case for privatisation of mining to deal
with the shortage of Coal in a sustained
manner;
(b) whether this issue was discussed at
a higher level meeting convened with the
representatives  from the Ministries of
Power, Steel, Railways, Fertilizers besides
coal users;
(c) whether Government have decided
to open up mining sector to private and
foreign investment and have approved Rs.
4000 crores of FDI in Coal sector; and
(d) if so, to what extent these decisions
would help to meet deficit in high value
minerals?
Coal production in the country
2403. SHRI  SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
Will the  PRIME  MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the demand of coal in the
country is fully met by the domestic
production;
(b) the details regarding the mine-wise
production and the country's annual
demand of coal; and
(c) the details of import of coal for the
last three years?
 Land allotted by SECL to ex-
servicemen
†2404. SHRI RAMADHAR
KASHYAP: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be  pleased to state:
(a) the number of houses, workshops,
shops and land allotted by S.E.C.L. to ex-
servicemen; and
(b) the details thereof and the basis for
allotting land acquired for the purpose of
coal mining?
Steps taken by Mahanadi Coalfields
for back filling and rehabilitation
2405. SHRI PYARIMOHAN MOHA-
PATRA:  Will the  PRIME MINISTER  be
pleased to state:
(a) the steps taken by Mahanadi
Coalfields  Limited for back filling and full
rehabilitation of excavated mines; and
(b) the reasons for very slow and tardy
progress in such rehabilitation and the
remedial measures proposed to be taken
thereon?
Availability of funds in mining sector
2406. SHRI JIBON ROY:   Will the
PRIME MINISTER  be  pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Coal India
Limited has posted a gross profit of Rs.
3700 crores in 2003-04;
(b) whether  Government are aware that
fund crunch  may lead to coal scarcity in
future; and
(c) if so, how Government propose to
meet the demand of fund in mining sectors?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Import of high quality coal
2407. SHRI  S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the  PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are importing high quality coal from
Australia and other countries;
(b) if so, whether such quality is not
available in the country;
(c) whether any effort has been made to
improve coal quality in the country;
(d) the exploration efforts going on in
this regard;
(e) whether any agreements been signed
with foreign companies to intensify the high
quality coal exploration efforts; and
(f) the details thereof?
VRS in BSNL and MTNL
†2408. SHRI  ABU ASIM AZMI:  Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be  pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
introduce voluntary retirement scheme in
Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd. and  Mahanagar
Telephone Nigam Ltd.;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that MTNL had
introduced voluntary retirement scheme for
its employees working in its offices situated
in Delhi and Mumbai;
(d) if so, present status thereof; and
(e) by when, Government would
completely ban voluntary retirement
scheme?
Development of C-DAC
2409. SHRI  K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:  Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY  be
pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is  a fact that the Ministry
in co-ordination with the C-DAC has
developed cyber forensic technique to deal
with the cyber crimes;
(b) if so, the details of the software tools
that have been developed by the C-DAC;
(c) whether the software tools also help
in analysing the other crimes, apart from
cyber crimes; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Public awareness programme in
Himachal Pradesh
†2410. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY  be  pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a proposal
regarding "Introduction of Information
Technology for Public Awareness in
Himachal Pradesh" had been sent to the
Additional Director, Department of
Information and Technology by the
Director, Information and Public Relations,
Himachal Pradesh vide their  letter dated
